groups.sentence: Instructors consider and raise AI bias and ethical issues with students before or at the start of a course.
Users identify, check and mitigate bias in AI output when using it.
AI detectors are more likely to wrongly flag non-native English speakers and neurodivergent students.
AI models reflect and can amplify biases from their training data and design, so outputs may be biased.
AI raises ethical concerns, including privacy, labor, environmental cost, access and misinformation.
Users are aware of and understand the potential biases and limitations of AI tools.
Everyone uses AI in ways that promote fairness, inclusion and diversity and reduce bias.
AI training data and tools can be unrepresentative and non-transparent, and can flatten or suppress diverse voices.
AI can produce offensive, stereotyped, racist or sexist content.
Administrators mitigate AI bias, evaluate AI systems for bias, and promote awareness of AI ethics.
AI may make biased or discriminatory decisions that treat people or groups unfairly.
Users must not rely on AI output that shows bias, and must not use AI in discriminatory ways.
Students consider the ethical and environmental impacts of using generative AI.
